full_judgment: 6. The present petitioners as the defendant Nos. 1 to 3 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter ilia, that the suit land of CS Khatian No. 185 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 216, Plot No. 70 originally belonged to one Hedaetullah who died leaving behind 4(four) sons among them Hasinur Rahman got 1/5th share of his father Hasinur Rahman died leaving behind the defendant Nos.1-3 as his heirs and they entered into an agreement for sale with the plaintiff on 1-3-1993 in respect of 18 decimals land out of 62 decimals as mentioned in the said agreement at a consideration money of Taka 3,65,000 and on 1-3-1993 they received 20,000 as advance. Both the parties agreed that the plaintiff would pay the rest of consideration money within 3-5-1993 and the defendants would execute sale deed and if the plaintiffs fail to do so the advance so paid would be forfeited. The agreement for sale as produced by the plaintiff before the learned Court, wherein plot number mentioned as 71 instead of 70, was not the real agreement for sale. The land of Plot No. 70 is the suit property of the agreement and the Plot No. 71 was recorded in separate CS Khatian No. 184 and SA Khatian No. 215 which is not suit property of agreement. The plaintiff failed to comply with the condition of the agreement dated 1-3-1993 to pay the rest of the consideration amount and that on 16-5-1993 plaintiff paid Taka 50,000 to the defendant No.1, and requested to extend time upto 15-7-1993 for executing sale deed and accordingly on 16-5-1993 an agreement for sale was executed on condition that if plaintiff fails to pay rest of the consideration amount the advance would be forfeited. On 15-7-1993 because of illness of the defendant No.1 sale deed having not been executed, with both side's consent time for executing sale deed was extended upto 15-11-2993 by writing the same on the over page of agreement dated 16-5-1993.
